newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA CRISIS DELAYS 1 MLN BBLS CRUDE CARGOES.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA CRISIS DELAYS 1 MLN BBLS CRUDE CARGOES.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company said Wednesday it declared force majeure on liftings at the Caribbean port at Covenas and that two cargoes of 500,000 barrels each had been delayed.
An Ecopetrol spokesman said the two shipments had been destined for the United States but declined to say who the intended buyers were.

As early as Tuesday Ecopetrol insisted it had not taken any decision on defaulting on its loadings schedules but New York traders said force majeure was effectively in place with at least one cargo, scheduled for Aug 6-8 loading, cancelled.

The Ecopetrol spokesman said all crude supplies at the 2 million barrel capacity storage facilities had been exhausted. The pipeline which pumps crude from the Cano Limon field in northeast Arauca province has been out of action for a week after a wave of rebel attacks and a landslide.

The spokesman said one rupture, caused by an explosion over the weekend, 218 miles (350 km) west of Cano Limon had already been repaired and that work was underway at the site of the landslide 79 miles (127 km) west of the field. Repair teams are still unable to begin work on the third break, 41 miles (67 km) west of Cano Limon, fearing the area may be mined.
Occidental Petroleum Corp OXY.Nu, the main Cano Limon operator, shut-in production and declared force majeure in the field Monday -- the second time in three weeks.
